# Authentication

## Endpoint

```
https://api.onesource.io/federation/{chain}/graphql
```

Replace `{chain}` with the target blockchain:

| Chain | Endpoint |
|-------|----------|
| Ethereum | `https://api.onesource.io/federation/ethereum/graphql` |
| Base | `https://api.onesource.io/federation/base/graphql` |
| Optimism | `https://api.onesource.io/federation/optimism/graphql` |
| Avalanche | `https://api.onesource.io/federation/avax/graphql` |
| Sepolia (testnet) | `https://api.onesource.io/federation/sepolia/graphql` |
| Shape | `https://api.onesource.io/federation/shape/graphql` |

## API Key

All requests require an API key passed via the `x-bp-token` HTTP header:

```
x-bp-token: BP-{YOUR_API_KEY}
```

**Key format:** `BP-` prefix followed by 24 alphanumeric characters (e.g., `BP-12345678912345678912345678`).

**Getting a key:**
1. Sign up at [app.onesource.io](https://app.onesource.io)
2. Navigate to your dashboard
3. Create a new API key

**Important:**
- The header name is `x-bp-token` (NOT `Authorization: Bearer`)
- Keys are prefixed with `BP-` (NOT `sk_` — that's the internal Mach10 API)
- Keys are chain-agnostic: one key works across all supported chains

## Subscription Plans

| Plan | Rate Limit | Notes |
|------|-----------|-------|
| Free | Limited queries/day | Good for testing and development |
| Starter | Higher rate limit | Production use |
| Pro | Highest rate limit | Enterprise workloads |

Check your current usage and plan at [app.onesource.io](https://app.onesource.io).

## CORS

The API supports CORS for browser-based requests. No additional configuration needed for client-side JavaScript.

## Quick Test

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.onesource.io/federation/ethereum/graphql" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-bp-token: BP-YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -d '{"query": "{ block(number: 19000000) { number timestamp } }"}'
```

If you get a JSON response with `data.block`, your key is working.
